compliance.environment: Indoor use only, in environmentally controlled areas

physical.material: Steel and aluminum with plastic T-shaped cable guides and plastic accessories

configs.description: The manager as Chatsworth ships 32610-E03, door fitted, without accessories.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the data sheet's cable fill row points to the maker's cable fill table on its site and states no figure; that table is not held.
the door opens to the right or to the left and lifts off; the format has no hinge, so it is drawn as one fitted plate and the side it swings from is not stated.
gaps.wanted: a format that can say a hinged cover

gaps.note: no held page dimensions a guide: the arm, the head and the width are read by eye from the page 1 photographs.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side view of one guide

gaps.note: the data sheet says the guides align with rack units and gives no count; 48 a side is the nominal 84 in over one rack unit.
gaps.wanted: the number of rack units the manager spans

gaps.note: the matrix prints the width (6 in) and the height (7 ft) as sizes to order by; only the depth is printed as an overall figure, so the width and the height are drawn at their nominal values.
gaps.wanted: an overall width and height, or a dimensioned drawing

gaps.note: the data sheet and the installation drawing show an integral central track and no held page gives its width or how far it stands from the rear; it is drawn as a strip the full depth of the frame.

no held page dimensions a side assembly: it is drawn as a plate 1.5 thick under its guides, the length of the manager and the width of a guide, which is an estimate; the guides stand on it and in front of the central section.

the manager ships with accessory rods, rotating fingers, cable bundle swivels and half spools (the data sheet, page 1; none on the 6 in and 8 in widths for the fingers and spools), which fit anywhere on the track; none has a fixed place, so none is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of a manager as shipped, with the accessories placed

gaps.note: the data sheet (page 1, key features) names a hook on the inside of the front door for a test meter, in text only. The installation figure (page 3) shows a hinge lug and the rear door's latches, not a hook. The hook is not drawn on the door's back because no held picture shows it.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the inside of the front door

gaps.note: the page 1 photographs, the page 3 render and the installation drawing (page 1) show a plate and two seams on the door. They sit at places that do not agree in millimetres at any listed width. The plate and seams are drawn on the 10 in width only, so they are not drawn on this one.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the door's face at this width

gaps.note: the page 3 render shows holes on the side plate, two above and one below. The page 1 photograph of the left-hand manager shows dots there. No held page gives their size or place. They belong to each device's own frame part, which a following change draws, so they are not drawn here.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned view of the side plate

gaps.note: the page 1 photograph of the left-hand manager and the page 3 render show a row of rungs down the central track, beside the door. No held page gives their pitch or size. They belong to each device's own frame part, which a following change draws, so they are not drawn here.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned view of the central track

gaps.note: the end caps and the feet show above and below the door in the data sheet's page 1 photograph. The door plate is drawn to the full nominal height over the guides. It hides them in the front elevation, and no held page gives the overall height with them.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned elevation with the caps and the feet

gaps.note: the door is drawn as a flat plate 3 mm thick at the front of the printed 392 mm depth; no held page gives its section. The frame, the guides and the door stand in a well 392 deep, open at the rear.
the manager attaches to the rack with carriage bolts; how far it stands from the upright and whether it overlaps the rail is never dimensioned.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the manager fitted to a rack

gaps.note: the matrix says only Glacier White; the shade drawn is chosen, and no held page gives a colour value.

gaps.wanted: `attrs.physical.weight-kg` (profile `passive` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - material, finish and the indoor-only statement are the specifications table (page 1): 'Steel and aluminum with plastic T-shaped cable guides and plastic accessories', 'Black or Glacier White powder coat paint'. The matrix (page 3) gives the colour of this part and its black fingers.

bottom.note: estimated - the bottom end is the top end again.

chassis.note: estimated - 150 mm wide, 2133.6 mm (7 ft, 84 in) high and 392 mm deep. THE DEPTH IS THE DATA SHEET'S (matrix note, page 3: 'Overall depth for Single-Sided manager is 15.5"D (392 mm)'); THE WIDTH AND THE HEIGHT ARE NOMINAL (matrix, page 3: 6" (150) and 7' (2.1)), taken here as the overall size, which the matrix does not say they are. The section is therefore estimated as a whole, and the figure of each dimension is in the entry that uses it.

color.note: estimated - 'Glacier White' (matrix, page 3); the shade is the near-white of the data sheet's page 1 photographs of a white manager, which are renders and not a colour value. The guides are black on every part number of this style.

door.note: estimated - the door's size and section. The data sheet (page 1) lists one dual-hinged front door assembly, pre-installed, drawn as one plate the height of the manager (installation instructions, page 3). It opens to the right or to the left and lifts off; the format has no hinge, so the side is a gap. The door has two latches on its back, in the door component's notes. The plate and seams are drawn on the 10 in width only.

ends.note: estimated - the data sheet (page 1) photograph shows 2 caps on the top end. It also shows 2 feet with a base plate and 2 small holes on the bottom end. The installation instructions (page 3) draw 4 hinge tabs on the corners of the door's back. Down the manager, a figure is photograph rows times 2.804 mm per pixel, the nominal height over the door's 761 pixels. Across it, a figure is the fraction of the door's 86 pixel width times this width, to 0.1 mm. A cap is 0.425 of the width and 25 tall. A foot is 0.19 of the width and 13 tall. The base plate is 8 tall. A tab is 0.07 of the width and 50 tall, from the figure's door, which is not to scale. The same figure shows a cross plate at each end of the door's back, 0.874 of the width and 116 tall. It also shows a rib 0.045 of the width between them. Both are drawn as outlines, as the figure draws them. No page gives a depth: each is half its width, a stand-in. The nominal height is taken as overall, so they stand over the ends of the body. The caps and the base take the door's colour; the pads and the feet are the photograph's sampled dark. The rear draws the caps, feet, base, tabs, plates and rib. The top draws the caps and their pads. The bottom draws the feet, the plate and its holes. The sides draw the caps, feet and base. The front door plate hides them there, so the front shows none.

fingers.note: estimated - A GUIDE TO EACH RACK UNIT, 48 A SIDE. The data sheet (page 1) says the side assemblies carry T-shaped cable guides 'that align with rack-mount unit (U) spaces on rack'; no page counts them. 48 is the nominal 84 in over 1.75 in, a column from the foot to the top of the manager. A guide is an arm 12 high with a head 30 high and 20 wide, read by eye from the page 1 photographs and taken to be the same on every width.

front.note: estimated - the door, fitted. With it off the front is the channel between the two side assemblies, the heads of the guides down each edge and the central track between them. The channel is 110 wide, the nominal 150 less a side assembly of 20 each side, which is an estimate.

guides.note: estimated - the duct on the front view is the channel between the two side assemblies, 110 wide, run down the height (`run: y`). Its finger pitch is the rack unit, 44.45; the gap between arms is the pitch less the arm's estimated 12.

left.note: estimated - the side, rear at x=0: 48 arms and heads at one rack unit and the door at the front. The side is open between the arms, as the data sheet's photographs show a side of slots.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE DATA SHEET'S ORDERING MATRIX; THE CONSTRUCTION FROM ITS TEXT AND THE INSTALLATION DRAWINGS. The Motive Cable Management data sheet (MKT-60020-675, 09/24) (page 3) builds the part number 32610-E03 from a style (1, single-sided, black fingers), a width (6 in, 150 mm), a colour (Glacier White) and a height (7 ft), and prints one overall depth for a single-sided manager, 15.5 in (392 mm). THE WIDTH AND THE HEIGHT ARE NOMINAL: the matrix prints them as sizes to order by, not as overall dimensions, and the figures here are taken as the overall size. The page 1 specifications and the installation instructions (IIS-737610) say what the manager is made of and how it is mounted and fitted with its door. NO HELD PAGE DIMENSIONS THE PART INTERNALLY: a guide, a side assembly, the track and the door are estimated, each in its own entry below. Nothing was copied from a picture; the figures are transcribed.

mount.note: drawing - rack-side. The installation instructions (page 2) have the manager positioned next to the rack and attached with 4 M8 carriage bolts, washers and flange nuts at the upper and lower pairs of holes (the kit holds 8 of each, instructions page 1), so it stands beside the rack. That its guides face forward is not stated by a held page and is drawn so. It occupies no rack unit; `ru: 48` is the 7 ft height over one rack unit and is estimated, because no held page says which racks a Motive height is for.

rear.note: estimated - the rear is open: the data sheet (page 6) sells a Rear Panel Kit that 'encloses the rear of the Motive Single-Sided Vertical Cable Manager', so none is fitted here. It is drawn as the back of the door seen between the two side assemblies and the central track; no held page dimensions the track.

right.note: estimated - the left view mirrored: the manager is the same on both sides.

shell.note: drawing - a hollow manager, as every manager in the library is. The body is a sheet body and its views are elevations; the solid is what its parts build: the frame, the guides on both sides and the door that lifts off and opens the front.

thickness.note: estimated - no held page states a wall gauge. 1.5 is the plate of comparable parts in the library; the parts carry their own thicknesses.

top.note: estimated - the end of the manager seen from above, rear at y=0: the side assemblies and the track to 389, the heads of the guides from 375 and the door to 392. The 392 is the data sheet's; the split is the estimate of the guide and the frame.
